Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for name certification and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is established; notarial deed executed before a Spanish Notario; CIRCE/CREyS electronic window as the single point of entry.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Consolidated Text of the Spanish Capital Companies Act), Articles 20, 21, 22, 23, 62, 112, 175, 210 to 229 and 266; Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Commercial Registry Regulations); Law 14/2013 (entrepreneur support) for the DUE/CIRCE electronic procedure.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation), followed by the hoja registral inscription in the Commercial Registry; the company acquires legal personality only upon registration.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 25 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

SL minimum share capital is €3,000 (Article 4 of RDL 1/2010), fully subscribed and paid-up in cash or in-kind at incorporation; the capital deposit must be certified by a Spanish credit institution (certificado de depósito), and is released upon registration; no separate escrow agent is required for the formation stage.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety compliance under Real Decreto 2267/2004 for fire-protection installations in non-industrial premises, including portable extinguishers, emergency lighting, and emergency exits; a structural-load certificate per CTE-DB-SE where any server room or heavy archive equipment is installed; occupational health and safety assessment under Law 31/1995 (Prevención de Riesgos Laborales), including the appointment of a prevention service, workplace risk evaluation, employee health surveillance, and registration of the centro de trabajo with the competent labor authority.

Paid-in capital rule: SL minimum share capital is €3,000 (Article 4 of RDL 1/2010), fully subscribed and paid-up in cash or in-kind at incorporation; the capital deposit must be certified by a Spanish credit institution (certificado de depósito), and is released upon registration; no separate escrow agent is required for the formation stage.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING BOARD OF [COMPANY NAME], SL: The subscribers and founding directors, acting unanimously, resolve: (1) to ratify the subscription and full payment of the share capital of €3,000 divided into 3,000 indivisible quotas of €1 par value, certified by the deposit certificate issued by Banco [X]; (2) to adopt as the registered office Calle [address], Madrid, within Spanish territory, where corporate records and legal notifications shall be kept; (3) to appoint [Name] as sole Managing Director with full corporate, banking, and representation powers; (4) to authorize the Managing Director to execute all filings before the Commercial Registry, AEAT, SEPBLAC, and municipal authorities and to implement the AML compliance regime required by Law 10/2010. Adopted and signed.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC) under Banco de España supervision, together with the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for obliged-entity registration; the municipal council for the activity licence; no industrial manufacturing authority applies to an office-based advisory boutique.

Category: Statutory registration as an obliged entity under Law 10/2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, coupled with the municipal Licencia de Actividad / Declaración Responsable de Apertura (local establishment operating permit); no sectoral investment-services licence is required for pure M&A advisory where no investment advice or order execution is provided, but corporate-finance advisory triggers AML registration.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), operating through the Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria. Regional tax authorities administer certain taxes in the Basque Country and Navarra under their respective Economic Agreement regimes; an entity resident in ordinary Spanish territory generally registers with AEAT.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Spanish Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) through AEAT using Form Modelo 036. A provisional NIF may be requested after execution of the incorporation documents and before registration in the Commercial Registry; the definitive NIF must be obtained after registration, generally by filing the registry documentation and updated corporate particulars. A foreign shareholder or foreign corporate director requiring Spanish tax identification must obtain an NIF, normally by filing Modelo 036 through an authorized representative, Spanish consulate, or AEAT office, with legalized or apostilled constitutional documents, official Spanish translation where required, evidence of existence and address, identification of the legal representative, and power of attorney. The company must use its NIF on invoices, tax returns, banking and commercial documentation. Registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and activation of the VIES status are requested through Modelo 036 where intra-EU supplies or acquisitions are expected. VAT registration must be completed before commencing taxable activities or making the relevant intra-EU transactions; there is no general low-value exemption that postpones registration for an SL carrying on an economic activity.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Spanish Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) through AEAT using Form Modelo 036. A provisional NIF may be requested after execution of the incorporation documents and before registration in the Commercial Registry; the definitive NIF must be obtained after registration, generally by filing the registry documentation and updated corporate particulars. A foreign shareholder or foreign corporate director requiring Spanish tax identification must obtain an NIF, normally by filing Modelo 036 through an authorized representative, Spanish consulate, or AEAT office, with legalized or apostilled constitutional documents, official Spanish translation where required, evidence of existence and address, identification of the legal representative, and power of attorney. The company must use its NIF on invoices, tax returns, banking and commercial documentation. Registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and activation of the VIES status are requested through Modelo 036 where intra-EU supplies or acquisitions are expected. VAT registration must be completed before commencing taxable activities or making the relevant intra-EU transactions; there is no general low-value exemption that postpones registration for an SL carrying on an economic activity.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person. Available elective or qualifying regimes may include the consolidated tax group regime, the VAT group regime, the cash-collection VAT regime where statutory conditions are met, the ETVE regime for qualifying foreign shareholdings, the SOCIMI regime for qualifying listed real-estate companies, and other expressly regulated special regimes. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the Corporate Income Tax Law restrict deductions, impose inclusion outcomes, or deny relief for arrangements involving hybrid instruments, hybrid entities, imported mismatches, or branches. Election deadlines, ownership tests, substance requirements, and notification obligations must be reviewed for the specific regime.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

None. Spain has no general domestic VAT turnover threshold below which a business may remain unregistered. A person carrying on an economic activity must register before commencing the activity or making relevant taxable transactions. Separate registration or reporting can be triggered by intra-EU transactions, imports, distance sales, platform transactions, or special regimes. The €10,000 EU-wide threshold for certain intra-EU consumer distance sales and electronically supplied services is not a general Spanish VAT-registration threshold.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods dispatched from Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for exemption with a right to deduct input VAT where the supplier or an appointed intermediary completes the export and retains evidence of customs exit. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer is identified for VAT in another Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies invoicing, VIES validation, and recapitulative statement requirements. Services supplied to a business established outside Spain generally follow the B2B place-of-supply rule and are outside the scope of Spanish VAT when the customer is established outside Spanish VAT territory; this is not technically a Spanish zero-rated supply. Certain services connected with exports, international transport, and transactions outside the EU may qualify for specific exemptions. M&A advisory services require a transaction-by-transaction analysis, including customer status, place of establishment, fixed establishments, actual use and enjoyment rules, and any connection with exempt financial or securities transactions. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, business-use evidence, proper accounting, and compliance with the applicable domestic or non-established-taxpayer refund procedure.

  • Electronic export declaration filed through the customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
  • Customs release and exit confirmation, such as the electronic exit results or equivalent customs evidence
  • Commercial invoice and export contract or order documentation
  • Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, airway bill, or road consignment note where applicable
  • Evidence identifying the goods, exporter, consignee, destination outside the EU, and transport route
  • Proof of payment or accounting records supporting the transaction where relevant to audit substantiation
  • For intra-EU exempt supplies: customer VAT identification number, transport evidence, and correct recapitulative statement reporting
  • An inward remittance certificate is not a general Spanish VAT condition for export exemption; banking evidence may nevertheless support the commercial and audit record

Spain does not currently impose a universal real-time pre-clearance requirement for every invoice. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including taxpayers with turnover above €6 million, VAT groups, and entities in the REDEME monthly refund regime, to transmit specified invoice-register data electronically to AEAT, generally within four business days, subject to statutory exceptions. Royal Decree 1007/2023 establishes requirements for computerized invoicing and billing systems, including integrity, conservation, traceability, accessibility, and anti-alteration controls, with the VERI*FACTU reporting model. The implementation timetable has been amended by subsequent legislation and must be confirmed at the filing date. The Corporate Information Society Law framework also provides for mandatory electronic invoicing between businesses and professionals, subject to implementing regulations and phased effective dates. A Spanish M&A advisory SL should maintain compliant digital invoice records, electronic signatures or equivalent authenticity controls, audit trails, and AEAT-compatible data exports; it should not assume that every invoice requires prior digital stamping or real-time clearance.

Spain has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. AEAT may deny or reverse an exemption where customs exit, transport, customer status, place-of-supply, or accounting evidence is incomplete or contradictory. The resulting VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and applicable penalties may be assessed retrospectively, subject to limitation periods and procedural rules. Tax penalties may generally range from 50% to 100% of the unpaid tax for serious infringements and from 100% to 150% for very serious infringements, with the precise percentage depending on concealment, fraud, repetition, document falsification, or other statutory aggravating factors. Incorrect VAT invoicing or failure to maintain required records may attract separate fixed or proportional penalties. Deliberate tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold of EUR 120,000 for a tax period may constitute a criminal offense, with potential fines and imprisonment for responsible individuals. Customs infringements may produce additional duties, penalties, seizure, or loss of customs simplifications. Voluntary correction, cooperation, effective restitution, and compliant documentary retention may reduce or mitigate penalties where legally available.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a euro-area Member State with full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU and Law 19/2003 on Foreign Investment. There are no exchange controls, no prior authorisations, and no limits on profit repatriation or dividend remittance for EU/EEA investors. Non-EU/EFTA investments in critical sectors (defence, dual-use items, critical energy, communications, data infrastructure, media, and sensitive technology) are subject to ex-ante screening when the investor acquires control (generally >10% voting rights or decisive influence) or, in specified sensitive sectors, when the gross transaction value equals or exceeds EUR 500 million, pursuant to Law 8/2020 and Royal Decree 571/2023. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are freely remittable via banking channels but attract a 19% statutory Spanish withholding tax, reducible to 10%, 5%, or 0% under the applicable double tax treaty (e.g., Spain-Latin America conventions); no central bank 'good leave' certificate or tax clearance certificate is required.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Not applicable. Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation of export proceeds or service-fee receivables; invoicing in EUR or any foreign currency is unrestricted. However, statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the Bank of Spain applies to all residents: any single cross-border transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000 (or cumulative monthly transactions reaching that threshold) must be declared on the official 'Declaración de Operaciones' (balance-of-payments statistical form) within the reporting month. Additionally, cash movements into or out of the EU in excess of EUR 10,000 require a written customs declaration under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672, and business-related cash payments exceeding EUR 100,000 are prohibited under Law 10/2010 (Article 34).

Central bank supervision: Bank of Spain (Banco de España) acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); monetary and exchange-rate policy is reserved to the European Central Bank (ECB) per Articles 127-133 TFEU. Foreign investment screening is administered by the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investment (DGCIIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, and AML supervisory enforcement is exercised by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias) under Law 10/2010.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM as a supplementary SEPA/EUR collection rail; LOW as the sole treasury infrastructure. Authorised equity is EUR 18,300 (0.9% paid) and registration in the Registro Mercantil is required. For the escrow of M&A success fees, a credit institution (bank) is mandatory because Spanish EMIs cannot take deposits, hold third-party escrow balances, or provide FX hedging; only licensed EDEs (entidades de dinero electrónico) may issue e-money and execute payment transactions. Offshore/EEA EMIs must passport into Spain under the EU e-money regime; UK-based EMIs lost passporting rights post-Brexit and require a Spanish branch authorisation or an EEA-licensed entity. Counterparty and safeguarding risk renders the boutique's Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML profile incompatible with fintech-only holding of client consideration.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) chain opacity: shareholders are holding companies incorporated in low-tax jurisdictions (e.g., Delaware, Panama, Netherlands) with nominee directors or unadjudicated share registers.

Root cause: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) chain opacity: shareholders are holding companies incorporated in low-tax jurisdictions (e.g., Delaware, Panama, Netherlands) with nominee directors or unadjudicated share registers.

Defense evidence: Consolidated UBO disclosure per Law 10/2010 (identification of every natural person with >25% interest); notarised and apostilled share registers; original share transfer agreements; Registro Mercantil certificates; sworn source-of-wealth statements for each UBO; certification that no nominee/non-natural person conceals the beneficial owner; EU/UN sanctions screening output for all UBOs.
High-risk jurisdiction exposure: success fees originate from Latin American or Caribbean counterparties, including PEP-related entities, or counterparties based in FATF-listed jurisdictions.

Root cause: High-risk jurisdiction exposure: success fees originate from Latin American or Caribbean counterparties, including PEP-related entities, or counterparties based in FATF-listed jurisdictions.

Defense evidence: Executed engagement letters detailing cross-border M&A advisory services (ISIC 7020 / NAICS 523150); copy of the CNMV registration or ministerial exemption letter confirming the statutory investment-services licence; original invoices and closing statements; SAR/STR clearance certificate; PEP status declaration and risk-rating memo; evidence of enhanced due diligence performed on the client; sworn declaration of non-criminal provenance of funds under Law 10/2010.
Disbursement to unknown third parties: the SL instructs split payments of a success fee to multiple external advisors or intermediaries without a disclosed contractual nexus.

Root cause: Disbursement to unknown third parties: the SL instructs split payments of a success fee to multiple external advisors or intermediaries without a disclosed contractual nexus.

Defense evidence: Tripartite or consortium agreements listing each beneficiary with full legal identity and tax residence; detailed fee-sharing schedules and basis of calculation; copies of MT103 payment trails; each beneficiary's NIF/equivalent tax identification certificate; board resolution of the SL approving the treasury distribution; sworn statements of the disposing parties confirming the non-existence of money laundering.
Unusual transaction velocity: multiple high-value (EUR 500,000+) inbound wires and immediate onward distributions within the first six months of account operation, triggering STR suspicion.

Root cause: Unusual transaction velocity: multiple high-value (EUR 500,000+) inbound wires and immediate onward distributions within the first six months of account operation, triggering STR suspicion.

Defense evidence: Annual treasury and liquidity policy approved by the SL's board; internal AML/CFT procedures manual with escalation thresholds; source-of-funds documents (shareholder loan agreements, share premium entries, closing statements); bank statements of the originating entities; pre-notification of large transfers in writing; minutes of the compliance committee authorising each treasury operation.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

All inbound equity injections or shareholder loans must be routed by SWIFT MT103/MT103 STP (for USD/GBP/other currencies) or SEPA Credit Transfer (for EUR) to the SL's designated operational account at an authorised Spanish credit institution. The payment reference must clearly indicate the transaction nature: 'Capital Increase - Escritura No. X' for registered share subscriptions, or 'Prestamo Socios' for shareholder advances, with the supporting corporate resolution and notarial deed submitted to the bank before value date. Statutory compliance: (i) each inbound transaction >= EUR 50,000 must be reported to the Bank of Spain under the balance-of-payments statistical regime (form 'Declaración de Operaciones') within the month; (ii) a post-investment declaration to the Registry of Foreign Investments (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores) of the DGCIIN is mandatory for non-EU/EEA investors within 30 days of the capital increase, including investor identity, amount, and purpose; (iii) legalisation of funds is required for non-resident investors without Spanish NIF. Banks will require board resolution, updated books, and a certificate of inactivity/no AML flags from the remitting bank for any inbound sum above EUR 100,000.Success-fee and advisory disbursements are cleared via: (i) SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for cross-border payments in EUR, USD, GBP, or LATAM currencies, with strict referencing of the invoice and engagement letter; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) and SEPA Instant for EU/EEA EUR payments; (iii) Commercial or Standby Letters of Credit (Documentary Credits under ICC UCP 600) exceptionally for structured deals where the buyer requires a bank undertaking for deferred payment or earn-out milestones; (iv) domestic transfers via the Spanish retail payment system in EUR to local beneficiaries. No FX authorisation is required, but every outbound transfer >= EUR 50,000 triggers the Bank of Spain statistical declaration, and any cash component above EUR 10,000 is unlawful and must be refused. For USD-denominated success-fee settlements, the bank may require a tax certificate (modelo 296/193) for non-resident payees or a WHT exemption certificate under the applicable treaty.Deliverable FX Forwards (Outright Forwards) - OTC, executed with authorised Spanish credit institutions (e.g., EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL) under ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex; fully permissible for hedging forecast fee income without MiFID II classification because the SL hedges its own treasury exposure.Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - for currencies with onshore transfer restrictions or limited deliverability in the Spanish interbank market (e.g., USD/CLP, USD/COP, USD/PEN, USD/ARS), offered by large international banks resident in Spain or via EU branches; subject to internal credit limits and must be macro-hedged against specific invoice-level exposure.FX Swaps (Swap de Divisas) - including spot/forward rollovers and forward/forward swaps used to manage short-term liquidity positions in multi-currency operational accounts.Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) - permissible for long-term dollarised success-fee receivables or shareholder loans, exchanging EUR and USD fixed/floating interest streams with an authorised Spanish credit institution, with full ISDA documentation and regulatory capital implications assessed by the bank.Currency Options (European-style Plain Vanilla FX Options) - available for contingent M&A fee flows where the closing probability is uncertain; purchased on a premium-paid basis to cap adverse EUR appreciation without obligations.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM as a supplementary SEPA/EUR collection rail; LOW as the sole treasury infrastructure. Authorised equity is EUR 18,300 (0.9% paid) and registration in the Registro Mercantil is required. For the escrow of M&A success fees, a credit institution (bank) is mandatory because Spanish EMIs cannot take deposits, hold third-party escrow balances, or provide FX hedging; only licensed EDEs (entidades de dinero electrónico) may issue e-money and execute payment transactions. Offshore/EEA EMIs must passport into Spain under the EU e-money regime; UK-based EMIs lost passporting rights post-Brexit and require a Spanish branch authorisation or an EEA-licensed entity. Counterparty and safeguarding risk renders the boutique's Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML profile incompatible with fintech-only holding of client consideration.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 days following the 6th month after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for calendar year-end, by July 25).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 Tax identification number (NIF) of the entity. Enter the NIF assigned by the Spanish tax authorities; if not available, use the foreign tax ID and indicate the country. Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months; plus daily surcharge of €200 per day for delays exceeding 3 months. Interest of 3.75% per annum applies. Non-filing may result in a penalty of 50% of the tax due.
Box 2 Fiscal year start and end dates. Indicate the exact period covered by the return, typically 12 months. Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months; plus daily surcharge of €200 per day for delays exceeding 3 months. Interest of 3.75% per annum applies. Non-filing may result in a penalty of 50% of the tax due.
Box 3 Net turnover (Importe Neto de la Cifra de Negocios). Report gross revenue from advisory services, including success fees, net of VAT and discounts. Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months; plus daily surcharge of €200 per day for delays exceeding 3 months. Interest of 3.75% per annum applies. Non-filing may result in a penalty of 50% of the tax due.

Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months; plus daily surcharge of €200 per day for delays exceeding 3 months. Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed €250,000 per year or if the entity's net turnover exceeds €10 million. Master File required for groups with consolidated turnover ≥ €50 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not have a formal ESR regime, but anti-abuse rules (e.g., general anti-avoidance rule, substance-over-form) apply. For M&A advisory, the entity must demonstrate adequate personnel, premises, and decision-making functions in Spain to avoid being deemed a shell company under the EU ATAD and Spanish tax law.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the evaded tax, plus interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding €120,000 per year may lead to imprisonment of 2-6 years.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed during investigation.
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: Reclassification of income as Spanish-source, disallowance of treaty benefits, and imposition of 25% corporate tax plus 19% dividend withholding on deemed distributions. Penalties up to 150% of the tax understated.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they signed false declarations. In severe cases, criminal charges for fraud may result in imprisonment and travel bans.
AML (Anti-Money Laundering)

Statutory sanction: Fines from €60,001 to €5,000,000 for serious infractions under Law 10/2010. Criminal liability for money laundering (Art. 301 Penal Code) with imprisonment up to 6 years.

Director personal liability: Directors are personally liable for AML compliance failures. They may face criminal prosecution, travel bans, and disqualification from holding directorships.
Transfer Pricing Misreporting

Statutory sanction: TP adjustment with penalty of 15% on the adjusted amount, plus late interest. If documentation is missing, penalty of €1,500 per data item (max €15,000).

Director personal liability: Directors who sign false TP documentation may be held personally liable for penalties if they acted with intent or gross negligence.
